## Summary

The initial geometry of a heavy-ion collision is influenced by several properties of the
colliding nuclei, including quadrupole deformation, triaxiality, nuclear radius, and skin
depth. This poster examined how variations and fluctuations of these nuclear-shape
parameters modify observables related to elliptic and radial flow.

The study focused on the initial-state eccentricity and inverse transverse size,
investigating their dependence on nuclear deformation across different collision systems.
The results showed that fluctuations of the quadrupole deformation enhance the
fluctuations of these observables, while triaxiality fluctuations reduce the differences
between prolate and oblate nuclear configurations.
